back_translation: Then he led me out northward into the outer court and brought me to the group of chambers opposite the open area and opposite the building on the north side.
The building with the door facing north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
Gallery faced gallery in three tiers, opposite the inner court that was twenty cubits wide and opposite the pavement of the outer court.
In front of the chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide leading inward, a path a hundred cubits long, and the doors of the chambers faced north.
The upper chambers were narrower, because the galleries took more space from the lower and middle chambers.
For these were built in three stories and had no pillars like the pillars of the courts; therefore the upper chambers were set back further than the lower and middle ones.
There was an outer wall running parallel to the chambers along the outer court, in front of the chambers, fifty cubits long.
For the chambers on the outer court were fifty cubits long, while those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long.
Below these chambers was the entrance on the east side, for those who enter from the outer court.
Along the wall of the court on the south side, opposite the open area and opposite the building, there were also chambers.
There was a walkway in front of them, like the chambers on the north side; their length and width were the same, and their exits, layout, and doors were alike.
So too were the doors of the chambers on the south side: there was a door at the head of the walkway, the path running along the east wall, at the entrance to the chambers.

Then he said to me, 'The north chambers and the south chambers facing the open area are holy chambers, where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will place the most holy offerings—the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering—for the place is holy.

When the priests have entered, they must not go out from the holy place into the outer court until they have left there the garments in which they minister, for those garments are holy. They are to put on other clothes before they approach the area that belongs to the people.'
When he had finished measuring the inside of the temple area, he led me out by the gate facing east and measured the area all around.
He measured the east side with the measuring rod—five hundred reeds, all around.
He measured the north side—five hundred reeds, with the measuring rod.
He measured the south side—five hundred reeds, with the measuring rod.
He came around and measured the west side—five hundred reeds, with the measuring rod.
He measured the area on all four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate the holy from the common.
